elements.name: Client application
elements.description: Any program that speaks the Postgres wire protocol. Its startup user name selects its tenant.

elements.name: Operator
elements.description: Runs proxy instances, writes the static fleet config, reads health and stats, drains an instance with SIGTERM.

elements.name: Developer or reader
elements.description: Runs simulator scenarios from a seed, replays a failure from its printed REPLAY line, runs make test / chaos / bench.

elements.name: mini-gateway
elements.description: A proxy that speaks the Postgres wire protocol (simple-query subset) in front of one Postgres: a hard-capped connection pool lent per transaction, per-tenant admission with two CoDel modes, read coalescing, timer-free batching, an off-by-default retry policy, snapshot observability. Runs as N independent instances.

elements.name: Postgres
elements.description: One ordinary Postgres server. Sees at most the fleet's connection budget, all logged in as one role.

elements.name: Metrics and log readers
elements.description: A Prometheus scraper, an OpenTelemetry Collector, CSV files, log readers. They read exporters and merge across instances; no component knows about them.

elements.name: pgproto3 (from pgx/v5)
elements.description: Go package github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgproto3: Postgres wire message structs with Encode and Decode. The one external dependency, used for message encoding only.

elements.name: Shell and binary
elements.description: cmd/mini-gateway and internal/shell. Listeners, one reader and one writer goroutine per connection, bounded mailboxes, a deadline on every socket operation, the admin listener on its own port, signal handling. Makes no decisions: it posts events to the engine and performs the actions the engine returns.

elements.name: Shell and binary
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-shell`.

elements.name: Engine
elements.description: internal/proxy. One single-threaded, sans-I/O state machine per instance: events in, actions out. Holds the client and database connection tables and the request pipeline with its stage seams. The simulator and the shell drive this same code.

elements.name: Engine
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-engine`.

elements.name: Wire layer
elements.description: internal/pgwire. Everything that knows Postgres: framing, both session state machines, the query-cycle tracker, the statement classifier, the error contract. The only product package that imports pgproto3.

elements.name: Wire layer
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-pgwire`.

elements.name: Work vocabulary
elements.description: internal/work. Small plain types the cores are written against: tenant, unit of work and its class, share key, batchable flag, outcome. Carries no Postgres type. This is the extension seam for a second protocol.

elements.name: Work vocabulary
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-work`.

elements.name: Admission
elements.description: internal/admission. Rate gate, per-tenant queues with two selectable queue rules, adaptive LIFO, round-robin dispatcher with shares that bind under saturation, adaptive concurrency limit.

elements.name: Admission
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-adm`.

elements.name: Pool
elements.description: internal/pool. Hard-capped database connections, creation limiter, leases per transaction, the one breaker, the dirty-connection table.

elements.name: Pool
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-pool`.

elements.name: Coalescer
elements.description: internal/coalesce. Identical provably-read-only statements share one database read. Never writes.

elements.name: Coalescer
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-coal`.

elements.name: Batcher
elements.description: internal/batch. Timer-free: when a connection frees up, eligible queued single statements go out in one write. Off by default.

elements.name: Batcher
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-batch`.

elements.name: Retry policy
elements.description: internal/retry. A policy interface. Off by default; the other policy retries once, only when nothing reached the database, within a 10% budget.

elements.name: Retry policy
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-retry`.

elements.name: Observability
elements.description: internal/obs. Snapshot conventions, integer histogram, collector, fleet merge, health, and the exporters.

elements.name: Observability
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-obs`.

elements.name: Configuration
elements.description: internal/config. The config file, the static fleet block (instance count N; fleet budgets divided by N), and load-time validation that fails closed.

elements.name: Configuration
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-config`.

elements.name: Simulator harness
elements.description: internal/sim, internal/sim/simnet, fakepg, workload, simtest, cmd/mgsim. A deterministic single-threaded world: virtual clock, simulated byte streams, a fake Postgres, simulated clients, faults, replay. Test code; built before any proxy code.

elements.name: Simulator harness
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-sim`.

elements.name: End-to-end suite and load generator
elements.description: test/e2e and cmd/loadgen. Each scenario is written once and runs on the simulator (tier S) and on the real binary against a real Postgres (tier R). The load generator is open-loop.

elements.name: End-to-end suite and load generator
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-e2e`.

elements.name: Transport seam
elements.description: Dialer and byte-stream connection events and actions: open, bytes in, bytes out, closed. Knows no protocol. Two implementations: TCP in the shell, simulated streams in the harness.

elements.name: Client session table
elements.description: One entry per client connection: its wire state machine, tenant, transaction state, the single request it may have inside the proxy, and its bounded reply buffer.

elements.name: Database connection table
elements.description: One entry per database connection: its wire state machine, the query-cycle tracker, and who holds it.

elements.name: Request pipeline
elements.description: The fixed order every request takes, each stage a small interface: classify, reject list, draining, breaker, rate gate, coalesce, queue, lease, forward, release. Statements inside an open transaction skip from classify straight to forward on the connection the client already holds.

elements.name: Reply relay
elements.description: Streams database messages to the client (or to every waiter of a shared read) through bounded buffers, with back pressure in both directions. Never sends a short reply that looks complete.

elements.name: Failure classifier
elements.description: For every failure records whether any byte reached the database, and picks the error-contract row.

elements.name: Deadline table
elements.description: Every wait in the timeout budget, as deadlines on the injected clock; returns the next wake-up time as an action.

elements.name: Drain controller
elements.description: Sequences shutdown: stop admitting, finish transactions in progress within a bound, close idle connections, exit.

elements.name: Snapshot publisher
elements.description: Collects every component's Snapshot() between events and hands the copy to the collector.

elements.name: Framer
elements.description: Ours. Cuts a byte stream into messages (type byte, 4-byte length, body) whatever the fragmentation, down to one byte at a time; enforces a maximum message size.

elements.name: Codec boundary
elements.description: The only product code that touches pgproto3: decodes a framed body into a message struct and encodes structs to bytes. pgproto3's own blocking reader is not used.

elements.name: Client session machine
elements.description: Client-facing. Answers TLS and GSS requests with no, reads the startup message, finds the tenant by user, runs SCRAM-SHA-256 (server side) or trust, sends the parameter set and proxy-issued key data, recognises cancel requests, takes in one query at a time, handles terminate.

elements.name: Database session machine
elements.description: Database-facing. Startup, SCRAM-SHA-256 (client side), collects server parameters and key data, reaches ready.

elements.name: Query-cycle tracker
elements.description: Follows a reply to its ReadyForQuery, reports the transaction status byte (idle, in transaction, failed), flags an unsolicited ParameterStatus (the connection is now dirty) and any protocol surprise.

elements.name: SCRAM-SHA-256 functions
elements.description: Pure functions on the standard library. Shared with the simulator's fake Postgres and test clients.

elements.name: SQL lexer
elements.description: Tokens only: strings, escape strings, dollar quotes, comments, identifiers; splits a message into statements. Not a parser.

elements.name: Statement classifier
elements.description: Turns a statement into a work unit: rejected (session-level feature), transaction control, provably read-only, shareable with its key, batchable. Conservative: what it cannot tokenise is never shared or batched.

elements.name: Error contract and reply builders
elements.description: One table: each refusal and failure, its SQLSTATE, whether anything reached the database, whether a write may have applied. Builds the ErrorResponse and the correct end marker. docs/error-contract.md is generated from it.

elements.name: Rate gate (GCRA)
elements.description: Optional outer gate, off by default: a per-tenant rate and burst in integer nanoseconds. Refuses before anything is queued. Rates are divided by the instance count.

elements.name: Tenant table
elements.description: State for tenants that are active now: queue, in-flight count, share, gate state. Created on first use, removed when all-zero, so memory follows active tenants.

elements.name: Per-tenant queues
elements.description: A fixed-capacity ring per tenant. Age is measured on the oldest item; expired items are swept from the head and answered at once; overflow sheds the head. Serves newest-first while the rule reports overload (adaptive LIFO).

elements.name: QueueRule
elements.description: The interface both shedding rules implement; chosen by config.

elements.name: Timeout rule
elements.description: Mode 1, from "Fail at Scale": one last-empty timestamp per queue; allowed wait is the short target while a standing queue exists, otherwise the interval.

elements.name: Control-law rule
elements.description: Mode 2, from the CoDel paper and RFC 8289: sojourn above target for an interval starts dropping; next drop after interval / sqrt(count), in integer arithmetic.

elements.name: Comparison arms
elements.description: Simulator only: plain FIFO and folly's minimum-delay detector, for the head-to-head table.

elements.name: Dispatcher
elements.description: Chooses whose request runs next: round robin across tenants with waiting work; a tenant's share binds only when the limit is reached; otherwise work-conserving.

elements.name: Adaptive limit (AIMD)
elements.description: One integer limit on concurrent leases. Cut by a tenth on a slow statement, a timeout or a connection failure; raised by one when busy. Bounded by a floor, the pool size, a maximum step and a minimum interval. Reads database round-trip time, never queue wait.

elements.name: Admission snapshot
elements.description: Snapshot(): per tenant and total — depth, oldest-item age, queue-wait histogram, rule state, LIFO switches, sheds by reason, in flight, share, limit and its changes, gate refusals.

elements.name: Connection accounting
elements.description: Every database connection is connecting, idle, lent or closing. Invariant: open + connecting never exceeds the pool size, which is the fleet budget divided by the instance count.

elements.name: Creation limiter
elements.description: Caps concurrent connects and the rate of new connections, so a storm or a cold start cannot flood the database.

elements.name: Lease table
elements.description: Lends a connection for one transaction: held while the status byte says in-transaction or failed, released on idle. Enforces the idle-in-transaction deadline.

elements.name: Database-down breaker
elements.description: The one circuit breaker. Counts connection-class failures only, never SQL errors. Open: requests are refused at once and no dial is made. Half-open: one trial connect.

elements.name: Dirty-connection table
elements.description: What to do with a connection whose client vanished or that surprised us: cancel, wait a bounded time, roll back, then reuse only if it is idle and clean; otherwise close. Destroy on doubt.

elements.name: Idle and lifetime reaper
elements.description: Closes idle and old connections, with jitter so they do not all expire together; checks a long-idle connection before reuse.

elements.name: Cancel map
elements.description: Maps proxy-issued key data to the connection a client currently holds, so a client's cancel request reaches its own statement and no one else's. Caps concurrent cancels.

elements.name: Pool snapshot
elements.description: Snapshot(): open, idle, lent, connecting, creation rate, closes by reason, exhaustion events, breaker state and transitions, dirty-table outcomes, lease-time histogram.

elements.name: Join rule
elements.description: Decides whether a shareable request leads a new read or joins one. Strict (default): never join a read already running on the database — join the next one, which starts when the running one ends. Relaxed: join the running read.

elements.name: Flight table
elements.description: In-flight and pending shared reads, keyed by the exact statement text. At most one read per key is on the database at a time. Entries are removed on completion.

elements.name: Waiter set
elements.description: The callers of one flight, counted. Capped. A caller that leaves gets its own error and does not disturb the rest.

elements.name: Flight deadline
elements.description: The flight runs under its own deadline, not any caller's. The database work is cancelled only when the last waiter has left.

elements.name: Shared reply buffer
elements.description: The reply's message bytes, stored once and capped; each recipient gets them with its own end marker. Errors are shared too.

elements.name: Do-not-share list
elements.description: Keys whose reply was too large to share. Bounded and expiring.

elements.name: Coalescer snapshot
elements.description: Snapshot(): flights, hits, waiters per flight, cancellations, overflows by cap, shared errors, table size.

elements.name: Take rule
elements.description: When a connection frees up, takes what is already queued and eligible, up to a count and byte cap. One request with nothing else waiting goes alone at once. There is no timer.

elements.name: Eligibility check
elements.description: A request may be batched only if the classifier proved it is a single statement that is not transaction control, and its client is outside a transaction.

elements.name: Reply splitter
elements.description: Splits the replies in order at the end-of-reply markers and matches each to its requester.

elements.name: Poison rule
elements.description: If any end marker reports a status other than idle, the connection is closed and the remaining members get the may-have-been-applied error.

elements.name: Batcher snapshot
elements.description: Snapshot(): batch-size histogram, batched share, in-batch wait histogram, poison events, ineligible reasons.

elements.name: Policy
elements.description: The interface the engine asks: given this failure — did anything reach the database, is the breaker open, how much of the deadline is left — may it be retried.

elements.name: Off
elements.description: The default. Never retries.

elements.name: PreForwardOnce
elements.description: Retries at most once, only when nothing reached the database, only within budget, never while the breaker is open, never holding a queue slot or a connection while it waits.

elements.name: Retry budget
elements.description: An integer bucket: each first attempt deposits a tenth of a token, each retry takes one; capped, so credit expires. Retries stay at or below 10% of requests.

elements.name: Retry snapshot
elements.description: Snapshot(): attempts, retries, budget level, deposits, withdrawals, exhaustions, refusals by reason.

elements.name: Event loop
elements.description: One thread, one heap ordered by (time, sequence), opaque events. Step budget, stall errors, panic guard.

elements.name: Virtual clock and timers
elements.description: 64-bit nanoseconds, cancellable timers. Time moves only when the loop moves it.

elements.name: Named random streams
elements.description: One generator per (seed, label), so a new draw in one place does not shift any other.

elements.name: Simulated byte streams
elements.description: internal/sim/simnet. Ordered byte connections with chosen fragmentation (down to one byte), latency per direction, a bounded send window, half-close, reset, stall, half-open.

elements.name: Fake Postgres
elements.description: internal/sim/fakepg. Speaks the simple-query subset in real wire bytes; connection limit; transaction status; a small keyed table with a write log; service-time models; every database-side fault; its own snapshot.

elements.name: Clients and tenants
elements.description: internal/sim/workload. Simulated clients: tenants, open-loop arrivals measured from intended send time, Zipf keys, transactions, disconnects, cancels, aggressive retries.

elements.name: Fault schedule
elements.description: Timed faults recorded in the trace; decodable from bytes for the fuzzer; a delete-one-fault shrinker. Faults are injected only from outside the proxy code.

elements.name: Decision trace and digests
elements.description: Every decision (accepted, coalesced, shed, timed out) appended in order; separate digests for the trace and for final state. Same seed, same digests.

elements.name: Invariants
elements.description: Checked at every event: connection cap, conservation of requests. Checked at the end: quiesce (nothing in use, nothing queued, no flight, no timer).

elements.name: Seeds, replay, sweep
elements.description: internal/sim/simtest. Seed flags and pinned seeds, the run-twice check, sweeps, the REPLAY line printed on every failure.

elements.name: cmd/mgsim
elements.description: Runs a named scenario from a seed outside go test and prints the digests.

elements.name: Toy echo protocol
elements.description: A tiny protocol with a planted-bug switch, used only to test the harness itself.

elements.name: Snapshot conventions
elements.description: What every component's Snapshot() returns: a plain struct of monotonic counters and current gauges. No wall-clock time, no map order, no telemetry imports.

elements.name: Integer histogram
elements.description: Fixed array, fixed relative error, no allocation on record; record, merge, percentile. Out-of-range values are clamped and counted.

elements.name: Collector
elements.description: Assembles one instance snapshot from the component snapshots, with instance id, build and config fingerprint. Keeps the last published copy; readers never wait on the engine.

elements.name: Fleet merge
elements.description: Merges instance snapshots: counters and gauges sum, histograms merge, ratios are recomputed, never averaged.

elements.name: Health
elements.description: Three states: ok; degraded while shedding, while the breaker is open, at the limit's floor, or draining; failed only when this instance cannot work. A database outage is degraded.

elements.name: Prometheus text exporter
elements.description: Low-cardinality labels and a bounded tenant label (configured tenants up to a cap, the rest as other).

elements.name: JSON stats exporter
elements.description: The full snapshot, including every active tenant.

elements.name: CSV writer
elements.description: Evidence tables for scenarios and benchmarks.

elements.name: Log-line exporter
elements.description: One structured line per interval.

elements.name: OTLP/HTTP push exporter
elements.description: Hand-written on the standard library, no SDK. Bounded queue, timeout, drop-and-count when the collector is down. Lands in the last build chunk and touches no component.

elements.name: Application hosts
elements.description: Clients of every tenant. They spread their connections over the instances themselves, or through any TCP balancer; we build none.

elements.name: Proxy tier, N = 3
elements.description: Three independent mini-gateway processes with the same static config: fleet.instances = 3, so each takes a third of every fleet budget. No instance knows about the others.

elements.name: Database host
elements.description: One Postgres. Its connection limit must cover the fleet budget plus a reserve; config validation checks it.

elements.name: Operations
elements.description: Where metrics are scraped or pushed to, and merged across instances.

elements.name: Client connections
elements.description: 500 clients here; each connects to one instance.

elements.name: mini-gateway instance 1
elements.description: Own engine, pool (fleet budget / 3), queues, flights, limit, retry budget and snapshots. Drains on SIGTERM.

elements.name: mini-gateway instance 2
elements.description: Own engine, pool (fleet budget / 3), queues, flights, limit, retry budget and snapshots. Drains on SIGTERM.

elements.name: mini-gateway instance 3
elements.description: Own engine, pool (fleet budget / 3), queues, flights, limit, retry budget and snapshots. Drains on SIGTERM.

elements.name: Postgres 17
elements.description: Sees at most the fleet connection budget (for example 3 x 32 = 96), all as one role.

elements.name: Scraper or collector
elements.description: Reads each instance's exporters; sums counters, merges histograms, recomputes ratios.
